title: Gauss–Jordan method for inverse of a matrix
summary: Gauss–Jordan procedure for a non-singular matrix and three worked inverse examples, including Grewal p. 39.
transcription_policy: Notebook wording and class-work order are preserved as far as safely readable. Strike-throughs and overwritten intermediate matrix entries are not treated as final values.

mapped_topics.label: Inverse of non-singular matrices by Gauss–Jordan method

blocks.text: This method is used to find inverse of non-singular matrix.
Let A be a non-singular matrix of order n. Write the given matrix with the identity matrix of order n.
Using only row transformations, reduce the A-side to the identity. The same row transformations applied to the identity side produce B, where B = A⁻¹.
The augmented-matrix reduction begins with a row interchange and continues on the next notebook page.
The left side is reduced to the identity matrix.
The class repeats the B. S. Grewal p. 39 augmented-matrix example.
The class writes A beside I, starts with \(R_1\leftrightarrow R_2\), and continues clearing pivot columns with row operations.
Several entries are crossed out and rewritten during the calculation.
The left side reaches the identity matrix.
